title: Profile of the mutual cost of two held sources on a hopping field

key_results.statement: Mutual cost $M(g_1,g_2)=E(g_1,g_2)-E(g_1,0)-E(0,g_2)+E(0,0)$, the part of the field cost in the stated state that depends on both $g_1$ and $g_2$.

Exact for all real $g_1,g_2$, every finite connected graph, $N_f\ge1$, $c=+1$, no pair terms among field objects: the lowest state is $\varphi_0(g)^{\otimes N_f}$ with no level crossing, $E=N_f\varepsilon_0(g)$, so $M$ is exactly $N_f$ times the one-object mutual cost; control: $c=-1$, $N_f\ge2$.

Second order (remainder $O(N_f|g_1g_2|(|g_1|+|g_2|))$, simple isolated lowest single-object eigenvector): $M^{(2)}=-2N_fg_1g_2\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\varphi_0|\Phi^{(1)}_{x_1}R\,\Phi^{(1)}_{x_2}|\varphi_0\rangle$, which for the class is $-2N_fg_1g_2\varphi_0(x_1)\varphi_0(x_2)R(x_1,x_2)$, with $R$ the reduced resolvent of $C_1$.

Second order, ring and tori, lowest state: $M^{(2)}=-(2ng_1g_2/t_f)\Lambda^+(x_1,x_2)$ with $\Lambda$ the graph Laplacian and $n=N_f/|X_f|$; $\sum_{x_2}M^{(2)}(x_1,x_2)=0$, so for $g_1g_2>0$ $M^{(2)}>0$ for some $x_2\neq x_1$.

Ring, second order, every $L\ge3$ and $d$: $M^{(2)}=\frac{N_fg_1g_2}{t_fL^2}[d(L-d)-\frac{L^2-1}{6}]$; for $g_1g_2>0$ strictly increasing on $0\le d\le L/2$ and negative iff $d(L-d)<(L^2-1)/6$; at fixed $n$ linear in $d$ for $d\ll L$ with a constant part $\propto L$.

Square torus, second order, $1\ll|\mathbf d|\ll L$: $M^{(2)}=-\frac{ng_1g_2}{\pi t_f}[\ln\frac{L}{|\mathbf d|}-\kappa_2]$, $\kappa_2=\ln\frac{\Gamma(1/4)^2}{2\sqrt\pi}=1.31053$, corrections $|\mathbf d|^2/2L^2$ and $O(|\mathbf d|^{-2})$; negative and increasing for $g_1g_2>0$; checked to $8.3\times10^{-3}$ in $M^{(2)}t_f/(ng_1g_2)$ for $L=64,128,256$.

Cubic torus, second order, $1\ll|\mathbf d|\ll L$: $M^{(2)}=-\frac{ng_1g_2}{2\pi t_f}[\frac{1}{|\mathbf d|}-\frac{c_3}{L}]$, $c_3=2.837297$, corrections $|\mathbf d|^2/3L^3$ and $O(|\mathbf d|^{-3})$; tends to $-ng_1g_2/(2\pi t_f|\mathbf d|)$ at fixed $n$; checked to $9.6\times10^{-4}$ in $M^{(2)}t_f/(ng_1g_2)$ for $L=32,48,64$.

Third-order mutual cost on a vertex-transitive graph, lowest state: $M^{(3)}=\frac{N_fg_1g_2(g_1+g_2)}{|X_f|t_f^2}[2\ell_0\ell_d+\ell_d^2-(\ell^{(2)}_0+2\ell^{(2)}_d)/|X_f|]$ with $\ell=\Lambda^+$ and $\ell^{(2)}=(\Lambda^+)^2$ entries.

Second-order form to relative accuracy $\epsilon$ (leading order, lowest state): ring $(|g_1|+|g_2|)L/10t_f\le\epsilon$ relative to $\max_d|M^{(2)}|$; square torus $(|g_1|+|g_2|)(3\ln L-\ln|\mathbf d|)/4\pi t_f\lesssim\epsilon$; cubic torus $(|g_1|+|g_2|)(W_3+1/8\pi|\mathbf d|)/t_f\lesssim\epsilon$, $W_3=0.252731$; independent of $N_f$ and $n$.

Exact eigenvalue equation for one field object with two sources: $(1-g_1\mathcal G_0(\varepsilon))(1-g_2\mathcal G_0(\varepsilon))=g_1g_2\mathcal G_d(\varepsilon)^2$, $\mathcal G=(\varepsilon-C_1)^{-1}$, for $\varepsilon\notin\mathrm{spec}\,C_1$.
Ring Green function: $\mathcal G_d(-2t_f\cos q)=\cos(q(L/2-d))/(2t_f\sin q\sin(qL/2))$, $0\le d\le L$, with $q=i\theta$ below $-2t_f$.

Ring, one field object, $g_1=g_2=g$, exact: $t_f\sin q\sin(qL/2)=g\cos(qd/2)\cos(q(L-d)/2)$, $\varepsilon_0=-2t_f\cos q$ (one source: $2t_f\sin q\tan(qL/2)=g$); for $L\gg1$, $ML^2/t_f$ depends only on $\gamma=gL/t_f$ and $d/L$ up to relative $O(L^{-2})$, and its expansion reproduces (4.5) and (4.8).
Ring and tori with even $L$, highest state, exact: $M_{\rm top}(g_1,g_2)=-M_0(-g_1,-g_2)$, so $M^{(2)}_{\rm top}=-M^{(2)}_0$ and the sign and monotonicity statements of (4.5)-(4.7) reverse.

Gapped control field (places $\{\varnothing\}\cup$ chain, $\Delta>2J$, $\Phi^c_x=|x\rangle\langle\varnothing|+$h.c.), second order, $|g_1|+|g_2|\ll\Delta-2J$: $M^{(2)}_c=-\frac{N_fg_1g_2}{J\sinh(1/\xi)}e^{-d/\xi}$, $\xi=1/\mathrm{arccosh}(\Delta/2J)$, faster than any power of $d$.

Bodies on a chain coupled to a ring field by $\pi$: the mutual cost is the same function of $d_0$ as of the graph distance up to a constant factor iff $\pi(m)=\pi(m_0)\pm k(m-m_0)\bmod L$, $k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, $kK\le\lfloor L/2\rfloor$ (sufficiency at all orders, necessity at second order); then $M=F_L(kd_0/\sigma_X)$.
The wrapping map $\pi(m)=m\bmod L$ on $K+1$ positions with $K>\lfloor L/2\rfloor$ fails (4.15), e.g. $M(0,L-1)=M(0,1)$ while $d_0=(L-1)\sigma_X$.

definitions.name: reduced resolvent of the single-object contract
scaled source strength on the ring
decay length of the control field
coupling map from chain labels to ring places

open_issues: Odd L: the highest state is degenerate and not fixed by connection; (4.13) is derived for even L only.
The tori conditions in (4.9) are leading-order estimates with O(1) terms not computed; no rigorous remainder bound beyond Kato's sufficient radius max|g_i| < 2 t_f sin²(π/L).
Long range is shown for the hopping class and short range for one gapped field; a general criterion over field contracts is not derived.
Field objects with c = −1, or with pair terms among them, are outside the class.
Necessity in (4.15) is shown at second order only.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: M2 ∝ g1g2/t_f and M3 ∝ g³L/t_f² are costs; γ = gL/t_f is a pure number
Ring L = 3 (complete graph): direct reduced resolvent gives M2 = 2 N_f g1g2/(27 t_f), equal to (4.5)
Ring L = 4: lowest plus highest state second-order mutual costs vanish at d = 1, 2, as (4.13) requires
